summary: Discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment requirements for Silverline Finance. Main concerns: cross-region constraints, private endpoints vs peering, egress/NAT, IP allowlists, KMS/HSM for keys, audit logs, and compliance evidence. Redwood AE+SE outlined Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and recommended Private deployment (VPC with Transit Gateway + PrivateLink where needed) for data residency and security. Agreed next steps: share network docs, SOC2 artefacts, schedule SE deep dive, and exchange CIDR ranges for pilot design.
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
Inter-region VPC constraints and region residency
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood — we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, just want to understand your network and security requirements for a private deployment. Samir and Rita from our SE team are here too.
00:12 Jordan (CTO, Silverline): Thanks, Alex. I'm Jordan, CTO. Priya, Marcus, and Tanya are on. We're evaluating Redwood because we need an inference platform that can live in our VPCs, meet our SOC2 and encryption needs, and keep latency low for trading signals.
00:30 Alex: Great — quick high-level question: are you leaning towards on-prem, cloud VPC, or multi-cloud?
00:37 Priya (Head of Infra): Primarily AWS, same account but multiple regions. We may have a GCP project for analytics, but production inference needs to stay in AWS us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for residency.
00:55 Samir (Redwood SE): Okay, good. So region constraints — we support Private deployments in specific regions today; we can run control plane in a Redwood-managed environment and data plane in your VPC, or fully customer-managed private control plane for stricter compliance.
01:14 Marcus (Security): When you say "data plane in our VPC" — does that mean you bring containers into our subnet? How does networking work, e.g., do we peer, or do you use PrivateLink? We're strict about no public egress.
01:27 Rita (Redwood): Good question. There are a few patterns: VPC peering (cross-account peering), AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints, or Transit Gateway attaching per account. Each has tradeoffs — peering is straightforward within region but doesn't cross regions, PrivateLink exposes a private ENI and is great for single-account access, and Transit Gateway scales better for multi-account/multi-region.
01:52 Jordan: We heard peering doesn't support transitive routing between regions — is that right?
01:57 Samir: Correct — VPC peering is non-transitive. For cross-region or multi-account scale we'd recommend Transit Gateway or PrivateLink depending on desired topology. There's also inter-region VPC peering but it's per-pair and can get messy.
02:12 Priya: We're trying to avoid NAT egress when possible. Can Redwood handle egress via our NAT gateways so outbound calls to whatever Redwood control plane need will be from our IP ranges? We have strict IP allowlists on firewalls.
02:28 Alex: Yes, you can keep egress through your NAT. In the usual private deployment we place inference nodes in your private subnets; outbound control plane calls to Redwood's control endpoints can go over the interface endpoints or via NAT — if you want deterministic IPs for allowlisting, you can route egress through a NAT or a set of egress proxies with fixed IPs.
02:48 Marcus: For KMS: we require customer-managed keys. Do you support CMEK with HSM-backed keys in our account?
02:56 Rita: We support KMS integration. For Private deployments we can use your KMS; keys remain in your account. For Hosted models we have a different flow, but for private the data encryption at rest and key wrapping can be done with your customer-managed keys.
03:10 Jordan: Audit logs and retention — we need detailed per-request logs for three years for compliance. Can you push logs to our S3 or CloudWatch?
03:19 Samir: Yes, we can forward audit logs to your S3 bucket or CloudWatch Logs. Retention is configurable on your side. Note that some debug traces may contain PII, so we'll mark sensitive traces; we also support filtering.
03:35 Tanya (PM): Latency is a big factor. If we run in our VPC with your inference runtime in our account, what kind of tail latency should we expect compared to Redwood hosted?
03:45 Samir: If you run the inference runtime in your VPC on similar GPU families, latency should be comparable to our hosted offering; the main delta is network path to the control plane for model fetches and telemetry. For strict low tail latency, we recommend local model caches and KV caching, which we can configure in the private deployment.
04:06 Priya: Regarding IP ranges — we'll need a list of destination prefixes for any service endpoints you require so we can add to firewall. Can you provide that?
04:15 Alex: Yes — we'll provide a published list of endpoints and recommended CIDR ranges. For PrivateLink we give you the ENI private IPs in your account, so no external CIDRs needed.
04:28 Marcus: What about bringing GPUs into our account? Does Redwood deploy AMIs/containers in our VPC or do you run managed instances that attach to our networks?
04:38 Rita: For Private we can either deploy our runtime as AMIs/containers in your account (you own the instances), or we can create dedicated instances that are in a customer-managed VPC but operated by Redwood under a managed tenancy. Most enterprise customers prefer the former to keep control.
04:58 Jordan: We have multiple accounts and use AWS Organizations; ideally we route everything through a central Transit Gateway owned by infra. Does Redwood play nicely with Transit Gateway?
05:10 Samir: Yes — Transit Gateway is a common architecture. We attach via VPC attachments; you can also use central shared services accounts and route traffic accordingly. We'll provide a reference design for Transit Gateway attachment and route tables.
05:28 Priya: Cross-account security: do you require cross-account IAM roles? How does onboarding work?
05:35 Alex: Onboarding typically consists of a CloudFormation/Terraform template that creates roles with least privilege (assume-role for operational tasks) and interface endpoints. We try to minimize cross-account privileges; for fully self-managed deploys you can avoid granting any long-lived cross-account roles.
05:50 Marcus: Encryption in transit — mutual TLS or mTLS?
05:54 Rita: We support mTLS for server-to-server traffic and TLS for external endpoints. For control plane we can do mTLS where keys are in your KMS.
06:05 Jordan: Our legal team will want to see SOC2 and any penetration test reports.
06:09 Alex: We'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts under NDA — I'll put those in the follow-up.
06:15 Tanya: How do you handle model updates/rollouts and rollback in Private? We need canarying because a bad model regressed trading signals in a past vendor pilot.
06:24 Samir: Rollouts are the same — Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts at the route level. In Private you can pin model versions and control rollout percentages; telemetry is routed to your internal logging.
06:38 Priya: DNS is a pain point — if we create interface endpoints, do you require special DNS entries? We have split-horizon DNS in our VPCs.
06:47 Rita: For PrivateLink we create interface endpoints which create ENIs and private DNS if you opt in; in split-horizon setups often customers opt to manage their own private DNS. We can provide CNAMEs or you can point your route53 private zones.
07:05 Marcus: Are there any ports that need to be open inbound? We are strict about ingress.
07:10 Samir: Typically only the control plane needs outbound to Redwood; the inference nodes accept traffic from your app inside the VPC on defined ports — those are internal-only. We don't require inbound internet-facing ports.
07:22 Jordan: What about model artifact storage — do we host model blobs or does Redwood host them?
07:28 Rita: You can host model artifacts in your S3 and we pull them using role-based access. Alternatively we can host them encrypted in our storage but for compliance customers often prefer to host in their S3.
07:42 Priya: For the pilot we want a minimal footprint in us-east-1 with one GPU cluster, private endpoints, and per-request logs going to our S3. Timeline is two weeks for proof of concept. Feasible?
07:55 Alex: Feasible — typical pilot is 2–4 weeks. For a 2-week pilot we'll need your CIDR ranges, a test account or role, and a list of success criteria (latency p95, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy on our eval set).
08:12 Tanya: Success criteria: p95 latency under 250ms for n=512 tokens, total cost under X (we'll quantify later), and no data leaving our infra.
08:22 Samir: Understood. We'll suggest model size and quantization profile to hit that latency.
08:30 Marcus: A few gotchas: our firewall egress goes through a central proxy so we need to whitelist destination IPs; also our compliance folks want proof of key handoff.
08:40 Alex: We'll provide IP ranges and KMS integration docs.
08:45 Jordan: Any limitations on GPU types? We mostly use p4d and g5 families in different clusters.
08:51 Samir: We support major GPU types; performance differs. For best throughput/latency we'd recommend A300-equivalent or p4. We can provide kernel/tuning guidance per family.
09:05 Priya: If we do cross-region, do you replicate model weights or use remote fetch? Replication affects disk usage and sync times.
09:15 Rita: Usually we recommend regional model replication for low-latency inference and to avoid cross-region egress. We can orchestrate model syncs as part of deployment.
09:28 Marcus: Regarding audit logs — can you redact PII automatically? We don't want raw PII in third-party logs.
09:35 Samir: We have masking rules and can filter out sensitive fields before logs leave your VPC. For private deployments we can keep all sensitive logs internal to your S3.
09:50 Jordan: Cost — is Private more expensive than Dedicated or Hosted?
09:55 Alex: Private often has higher operational overhead since you're hosting the instances, but it's comparable to Dedicated when you factor in reserved capacity. Hosted is cheapest for pure unit economics but doesn't fit your compliance requirements. We'll put a side-by-side cost estimate.
10:11 Tanya: Any experience integrating with our existing secrets manager? We use HashiCorp Vault for model credentials.
10:18 Rita: We integrate with Vault; for model pulling we can use short-lived creds that your Vault issues. We'll document the auth flow.
10:28 Marcus: Network ACLs: we have strict port ranges. Do you need ICMP or ephemeral ports opened?
10:34 Samir: No ICMP needed typically. Ephemeral egress ports for outbound connections are used but those are outbound-only and controlled.
10:44 Jordan: What about upgrades — how do we test runtime upgrades?
10:48 Samir: We recommend a canary pool and rolling upgrade plan; you manage the instances so you control scheduling, but we provide scripts and a recommended upgrade path.
11:00 Tanya: Could you give an example architecture for Transit Gateway with multiple accounts?
11:05 Alex: Sure — I'll share a diagram in the follow-up. High-level: each account's VPC attaches to the transit gateway; central infra account hosts shared services and route tables; Redwood runtime VPC attaches to the TGW and is reachable via route maps. For PrivateLink endpoints we create interface endpoints in the customer's VPCs.
11:28 Marcus: Are there additional compliance attestations for key escrow? We don't want keys leaving our KMS.
11:34 Rita: For Private we never escrow your keys — keys stay in your KMS. If you require HSM-backed FIPS modules we can accommodate via customer KMS in accounts that have HSM.
11:50 Priya: About DNS again — some of our teams use service mesh; will that interfere?
11:55 Samir: As long as your mesh allows for the internal ports and IPs we need, it's fine. We'll test with your infra during the pilot.
12:10 Jordan: Okay let's talk timeline — we want a pilot by end of month, two-week run. Are Redwoods calendar openings next week?
12:18 Alex: Yes. Samir, Rita — can you do a technical deep dive next Tuesday with Priya and Marcus?
12:23 Samir: Yep — I'll block it.
12:26 Tanya: For the pilot metrics we'll need your recommendations for model/quantization to match latency.
12:30 Samir: We'll propose a config in the follow-up with estimated token costs and CPU/GPU sizing.
12:40 Priya: We will provide CIDRs and an AWS test role by Monday.
12:44 Marcus: Also please include example CloudFormation/Terraform templates.
12:48 Alex: We'll include templates and an onboarding checklist.
12:52 Jordan: Any other gotchas we should be aware of?
12:56 Rita: One is model compatibility — if you're bringing custom models, we need to verify operator runtime compatibility and possibly recompile kernels. That can add time to onboarding.
13:08 Jordan: Good point — we have some custom quantized models. We'll flag that.
13:12 Tanya: Ok, let's summarize next steps — Jordan?
13:16 Jordan: We'll send CIDR ranges and a test role by Monday; we expect a follow-up deep technical session next Tuesday. Marcus will confirm firewall constraints.
13:24 Alex: And from Redwood we'll send the network diagram, SOC2 docs, templates, and initial cost estimate — aiming to send by end of day Friday.
13:32 Samir: I'll include an initial pilot architecture and performance tuning tips.
13:36 Marcus: Quick small question — do you support bring-your-own-license for the runtime?
13:40 Rita: We have BYO-license options in some contracts; we'll discuss in procurement if needed.
13:46 Tanya: Thanks everyone.
13:48 Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with artifacts and schedule the SE deep dive.
13:52 [call ends]
